skill_title: Solve vertical projectile problems with kinematic equations and graphs
notes: 20 items: 11 lifted, 9 fresh. Single-stage vertical projectile problems: free-fall definition, max height, time to max height, displacement, velocity at a given time, v-t and y-t graph reading. Multi-stage / bounce problems live in A2.

items.question: Give the definition of FREE FALL.
items.expectedAnswer: Motion of an object under the influence of gravity only (no air resistance or other forces).
items.explanation: Two marks: (1) 'motion of an object'; (2) 'under gravity only / no air resistance'. The defining feature is that gravity is the SOLE force.
options: Motion of an object under the influence of gravity only (no air resistance or other forces).
Any downward motion of an object toward the Earth.
Motion of an object that simply speeds up as it falls.

items.question: Define the term PROJECTILE.
items.expectedAnswer: An object moving under the influence of gravity only (no other forces).
items.explanation: Same idea as free fall — gravity is the only force acting. Distinguished from free fall by emphasis on a launched object.
options: Any object that has been thrown forward through the air.
An object moving under the influence of gravity only (no other forces).
An object that moves in a curved path because a force keeps pushing it along.

items.question: A 0.06 kg ball is thrown from a balcony and is in free fall. What is the magnitude of the ACCELERATION of the ball at t = 1.02 s? Give a reason for your answer.
items.explanation: 9.8 m·s⁻² downward. The only force acting is gravity, so the acceleration equals g throughout the flight — independent of position or velocity.

items.question: A ball is dropped from rest from the top of a building. It reaches the ground 3 s after being released. Calculate the height of the building. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻², downward positive.)
items.explanation: From rest, y = ½gt² = ½ × 9.8 × 9 = 44.1 m.

items.question: A ball is dropped from rest. Calculate the velocity of the ball 1.0 s after release. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻², downward positive.)
items.explanation: v = v₀ + gt = 0 + 9.8 × 1 = 9.8 m·s⁻¹ downward.

items.question: Disc C is thrown from the top of a 30 m building at 15 m·s⁻¹ vertically upward. Calculate the time for C to reach its maximum height. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻².)
items.explanation: At max height v = 0. Using v = v₀ − gt: 0 = 15 − 9.8t ⇒ t = 15/9.8 ≈ 1.53 s.

items.question: Disc C is thrown from the top of a 30 m building at 15 m·s⁻¹ upward. Calculate the maximum height of C above the GROUND. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻².)
items.explanation: Height above roof at max: v² = v₀² − 2gΔy ⇒ 0 = 225 − 2(9.8)Δy ⇒ Δy = 11.48 m. Above ground = 30 + 11.48 ≈ 41.5 m.

items.question: Ball A is dropped from rest from a height of 15.2 m. Calculate the time taken for A to hit the ground. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻².)
A ball is thrown vertically upward from the ground with an initial velocity of 25 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the maximum height reached. Take upward positive, g = 10 m·s⁻² downward.
items.explanation: At max height v = 0. v² = v₀² + 2aΔy ⇒ 0 = 625 + 2(−10)Δy ⇒ Δy = 31.25 m.

items.question: A ball is thrown upward at 25 m·s⁻¹ (g = 10 m·s⁻²). At what time(s) is the SPEED of the ball equal to 15 m·s⁻¹? (Use upward positive.)
items.expectedAnswer: t = 1.0 s (going up) and t = 4.0 s (coming down).
items.explanation: SPEED is the magnitude of velocity, so both +15 and −15 satisfy. By symmetry the two times are equidistant from the peak (t = 2.5 s).
options: t = 1.0 s only.
t = 2.5 s, at maximum height.
t = 1.0 s (going up) and t = 4.0 s (coming down).

items.question: A ball is thrown upward from the edge of a 45 m cliff with an initial velocity of 20 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the maximum height above the GROUND. Take upward positive, g = 10 m·s⁻² downward.
items.explanation: Max height above cliff: v² = v₀² + 2aΔy ⇒ 0 = 400 + 2(−10)Δy ⇒ Δy = 20 m. Above ground = 45 + 20 = 65 m.

items.question: A stone is thrown vertically upward. Which of the following is true at the highest point of its motion?
options: Velocity is zero and acceleration is zero
Velocity is zero and acceleration is 9.8 m·s⁻² downward
Velocity is 9.8 m·s⁻² downward and acceleration is zero
Velocity is upward and acceleration is downward
items.expectedAnswer: Velocity is zero and acceleration is 9.8 m·s⁻² downward
items.explanation: At the highest point velocity instantaneously becomes zero, but gravity is still acting, so acceleration is g downward throughout the entire flight.

items.question: A ball is dropped from rest. How does its velocity change with time on a velocity-time graph (downward positive)?
options: Horizontal line at v = 0
Straight line, positive constant gradient through the origin
Curved line bending upward
Straight line with negative gradient
items.expectedAnswer: Straight line, positive constant gradient through the origin
items.explanation: Constant acceleration (g) gives a straight line on a v-t graph. From rest ⇒ starts at origin. Downward positive ⇒ positive gradient.

items.question: On a velocity-time graph for a vertical projectile, what does the AREA between the curve and the time axis represent?
options: Acceleration
Velocity
Displacement
Force
items.explanation: Area under a v-t graph = displacement (or change in position). Gradient of v-t = acceleration.

items.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 30 m·s⁻¹ from ground level. Calculate the velocity of the ball when it returns to its launch point. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻².)
items.explanation: By symmetry, the ball returns to the launch point with the same SPEED as it was thrown — 30 m·s⁻¹ — but now moving DOWNWARD. (Magnitude unchanged when no air resistance.)

items.question: A ball is thrown upward and reaches its maximum height in 2.5 s. Calculate the initial velocity at which it was thrown. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻².)
items.explanation: At max height v = 0. v = v₀ − gt ⇒ 0 = v₀ − 9.8(2.5) ⇒ v₀ = 24.5 m·s⁻¹.

items.question: A stone is thrown DOWNWARD from a roof 25 m high at an initial speed of 5 m·s⁻¹. Find its speed when it hits the ground. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻², downward positive.)
A learner says: 'When the projectile reaches maximum height, the force of gravity is zero because velocity is zero.' Is this correct? Briefly explain.
items.expectedAnswer: Incorrect — at the peak v = 0 but gravity still acts (weight mg down, a = g down).
items.explanation: Common confusion. Gravity is always present; what changes is velocity. The acceleration is constant throughout the flight (g downward).
options: Incorrect — at the peak v = 0 but gravity still acts (weight mg down, a = g down).
Correct — with zero velocity there is no force on the projectile.
Incorrect — gravity isn't zero, but the acceleration is zero at the top.

items.question: A ball is dropped from rest. After 2 s, calculate (a) its velocity and (b) the distance it has fallen. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻².)
items.explanation: v = gt = 9.8 × 2 = 19.6 m·s⁻¹. y = ½gt² = ½ × 9.8 × 4 = 19.6 m. (Numerically coincide because t = 2; in general they don't.)

items.question: A ball is thrown up from the top of a tall cliff. On a velocity-time graph with UPWARD positive, what shape does the v-t graph have?
options: Horizontal line at the initial velocity
Straight line with NEGATIVE constant gradient
Straight line with POSITIVE constant gradient
U-shape (parabolic)
items.expectedAnswer: Straight line with NEGATIVE constant gradient
items.explanation: Acceleration is g downward (= −g with upward positive). Constant acceleration ⇒ straight line. Negative acceleration ⇒ negative gradient. Velocity starts positive, decreases through zero at peak, becomes negative as ball falls.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_FREE_FALL_DEF_INCOMPLETE: Free-fall/projectile definition missing 'gravity only / no air resistance'
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_ACCEL_AT_TOP_ZERO: Says acceleration is zero at the highest point
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_ACCEL_VARIES_WITH_T: Believes the acceleration in free fall changes during the flight
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_KINEMATIC_EQUATION_SELECT: Picks the wrong kinematic equation for the given knowns
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_SIGN_CONVENTION_VPM: Uses g = +9.8 with upward-positive convention (sign error)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_AT_TOP_V_NONZERO: Doesn't set v = 0 at the highest point in calculations
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_SPEED_VS_VELOCITY: Treats speed and velocity as the same
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_VT_AREA_MEANING: Reads v-t area as something other than displacement
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INITIAL_VELOCITY_SIGN: Drops the sign of initial velocity in downward throw
